cv-a877168d.stem: How many chambers does the heart have?
cv-a877168d.explanation: The heart consists of two atria and two ventricles. The right side pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs, the left side oxygenated blood to the body.

cv-94d9d190.stem: What is the double-layered sac surrounding the heart called?
cv-94d9d190.explanation: The pericardium is a sac with an outer fibrous layer and an inner serous layer (parietal and visceral). The endocardium lines the inside of the heart, the myocardium is the heart muscle.

cv-3db2d7ed.stem: Which valve lies between the right atrium and the right ventricle?
cv-3db2d7ed.explanation: The right atrioventricular valve has three cusps (tricuspid). Between the left atrium and left ventricle lies the two-cusped mitral valve.

cv-d1d99274.stem: Which valve lies between the left atrium and the left ventricle?
cv-d1d99274.explanation: The mitral valve has two cusps, anterior and posterior; they are attached by chordae tendineae to the papillary muscles of the left ventricle.

cv-26a232bf.stem: Which heart chamber has the thickest wall?
options: All four chambers have equal walls
cv-26a232bf.explanation: The left ventricle has the thickest wall because it pumps blood at high pressure to the whole body; it is about three times thicker than the right ventricle.

cv-d6a24725.stem: Which chamber forms the tip (apex) of the heart?
cv-d6a24725.explanation: The apex of the heart is formed by the left ventricle and is felt in the left 5th intercostal space just medial to the midclavicular line (apex beat).

cv-412b75c1.stem: What are the arteries supplying the heart muscle called?
cv-412b75c1.explanation: The right and left coronary arteries arise from the aortic sinuses at the root of the ascending aorta and supply the heart wall; their occlusion causes myocardial infarction.

cv-7d873071.stem: What is the heart's natural pacemaker called?
cv-7d873071.explanation: The SA node lies in the right atrium beside the opening of the superior vena cava and initiates the heartbeat. The impulse then passes to the AV node, bundle of His, bundle branches and Purkinje fibres.

cv-05cc936f.stem: From which heart chamber does the pulmonary circulation begin?
cv-05cc936f.explanation: The pulmonary circulation starts from the right ventricle with the pulmonary trunk and ends in the left atrium via the pulmonary veins. The systemic circulation starts from the left ventricle with the aorta.

cv-ec83a847.stem: Which is the largest artery distributing oxygenated blood to the whole body?
cv-ec83a847.explanation: The aorta leaves the left ventricle; through its ascending part, arch, thoracic and abdominal parts it carries blood to the whole systemic circulation.

cv-7e929d6e.stem: Which vessel carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs?
cv-7e929d6e.explanation: The pulmonary arteries are the only arteries carrying deoxygenated blood; they leave the right ventricle and go to the lungs.

cv-98ef52a0.explanation: The pulmonary veins bring oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium; they are the only veins carrying oxygenated blood.

cv-37cfee07.stem: What is the part of the aorta that curves to the left and backwards after leaving the heart called?
cv-37cfee07.explanation: After rising, the ascending aorta curves backwards over the left main bronchus at T4 to form the aortic arch; three large branches to the head, neck and arms arise from the arch.

cv-94dfc545.stem: Which artery is used to take the pulse in the neck?
cv-94dfc545.explanation: The carotid pulse is taken at the level of the thyroid cartilage along the anterior border of sternocleidomastoid; in emergencies it is the most reliable central pulse.

cv-f01b4115.stem: Which neck artery supplies the anterior and middle parts of the brain and the eye?
cv-f01b4115.explanation: The internal carotid artery enters the skull without giving branches in the neck; it supplies the eye through the ophthalmic artery and most of the hemispheres through the anterior and middle cerebral arteries.

cv-8d543b43.stem: What is the arterial ring at the base of the brain connecting the carotid and vertebrobasilar systems called?
cv-8d543b43.explanation: The circle of Willis links the anterior and posterior circulations and can provide collateral flow when an artery is occluded; most brain aneurysms develop on this ring.

cv-40ea677c.stem: The basilar artery is formed by the union of which arteries?
cv-40ea677c.explanation: The right and left vertebral arteries join at the pontomedullary junction to form the basilar artery, which supplies the brainstem, cerebellum and occipital lobe.

cv-02933170.stem: Into which two branches does the brachial artery divide in front of the elbow?
cv-02933170.explanation: The brachial artery divides in the cubital fossa, at the level of the neck of the radius, into the radial and ulnar arteries.

cv-0111f3a8.stem: Which artery is most often used to take the pulse at the wrist?
cv-0111f3a8.explanation: The radial pulse is easily felt on the thumb side of the wrist over the lower end of the radius.

cv-b50a69cf.stem: Into which arteries does the abdominal aorta divide at its lower end?
cv-b50a69cf.explanation: The abdominal aorta divides at L4 into the right and left common iliac arteries, which in turn divide into internal and external iliac arteries.

cv-a0f7e29b.explanation: The renal arteries arise from both sides of the abdominal aorta at L1–L2; about one fifth of the cardiac output goes to the kidneys.

cv-b6985d99.stem: Which is the main artery of the thigh?
cv-b6985d99.explanation: The external iliac artery becomes the femoral artery after passing under the inguinal ligament; it runs the length of the thigh and becomes the popliteal artery behind the knee.
